messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] continuous-batch: sudden latency cliff on runtime-pool-us-west-2 at high concurrency (>1200 req/s), trending since 00:02 UTC. Possible KV cache regen / microbatch pileup. Paging eng-oncall. :rotating_light:
jamie: acked. oncall taking. digging into prefeth/kvcache metrics now.
sasha: seeing KV cache evictions spike ~00:01:30, almost full regen. eviction rate 18k/min on node group `runtime-pool-3`. Also microbatch sizes jumped from 4->16 on hot paths, queue depth spiked.
mike: logs show a lot of requests stalled waiting for microbatch window:
```
2026-03-15T00:01:45Z runtime: awaiting batch slot (window_ms=15) id=xyz queue_len=132 microbatch_sz=16
2026-03-15T00:01:46Z kvcache: evict shard=7 bytes=512MB reason=pressure
2026-03-15T00:01:47Z runtime: emit latency 1200ms id=xyz
```
anya: confirmed some customers hitting 95th p50->p95 regressions, dedicated tenants A & C showing 8-20% errors and timeouts. downgrading to possible degraded state for SLA.
jamie: hypothesis: an orchestration change earlier (auto-batching tuning) increased target microbatch max_size; under high concurrency that creates fanout where many requests wait for large microbatches, KV cache pressure spikes and causes cascaded evictions -> regen -> stalls.
sasha: agree. telemetry shows microbatch size distribution shifted at 23:58 UTC when `cb.autotune.max_microbatch` bumped to 16 via rollout/1234.
mike: mitigation option 1: revert rollout/1234 (fast). Option 2: temporarily set fleet flag `cb.autotune.max_microbatch=4` and reduce `cb.window_ms` to 8 to avoid long waits. Option 3: throttle prefetch rate to reduce KV regen.
jamie: doing quick risk calc: revert rollout is simplest but may be slower if rollout is global. Flag flip is immediate if gating exists. We have a runtime flag that can be toggled via `/admin/flags` for all nodes in a region. I'll flip to 4 first.
jamie: running command: `curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/flags -d '{"flag":"cb.autotune.max_microbatch","value":4,"scope":"runtime-pool-us-west-2"}'`
deploy-bot: flag update accepted, initiating propagation to runtime-pool-us-west-2 (3 zones).
sasha: metrics starting to show microbatch distribution shifting back toward 2-6 within 30s. queue depth dropping from 130->40. KV eviction rate falling.
anya: customer impact: errors down to 3-6% from 8-20% for dedicated tenants after flag flip. Latency p95 trending down but still above SLO for a small cohort.
mike: follow-up: lower `cb.window_ms` to 8 to reduce waiting time for microbatches. I can patch a rolling config via the config service: `POST /cfg/runtime?pool=runtime-pool-us-west-2 {"cb.window_ms":8}`
jamie: go ahead mike. coordinate with Sasha for observed effects.
mike: applied config change, rolling to 20% -> 50% -> 100% nodes with 10s between stages.
sasha: early canary good: p95 down 30% on canary nodes, no error increase. Full rollout progressing. KV eviction down to baseline after full propagation.
anya: customer update: sent short note to support and affected account owners. We should track until next 2 hours and plan postmortem with timeline + root cause.
jamie: immediate mitigation complete. next steps: 1) rollback/patch of autotune rollout to prevent re-release. 2) add safety limiter: if queue_len > 100 then clamp microbatch max to 4. 3) add alert for microbatch-size-shift anomaly.
dan: i'm next oncall in 30m. please hand off state + actions taken.
jamie: handoff summary for @dan — Incident: continuous-batch perf cliff due to microbatch fanout causing KV cache evictions and regen. Timeline: 23:58 UTC rollout/1234 changed cb.autotune.max_microbatch->16; 00:01 UTC evictions spike; 00:02 pager fired. Mitigations applied: flag set cb.autotune.max_microbatch=4 at 00:07 (propagated by deploy-bot), cb.window_ms reduced to 8 at 00:09, full rollout by 00:12. Customer impact: dedicated tenants A/C saw 8-20% errors during peak; now reduced to 3-6%. Ongoing: monitor KV eviction rate, queue depth, p95 latencies for 2h; prepare postmortem with timeline and suggested hotfix (safety limiter + revert autotune rollout).
dan: ack. I'll monitor next 2h, I've added a dashboard with key graphs and alert thresholds. If anything regresses, I'll escalate to runtime leads. Also filing a postmortem stub.
anya: added notes to support thread and tagged account owners. prepping short RCA bullet points.
jamie: leaving channel, oncall handoff complete. thanks team :thumbsup:
dan: thanks all. closing pager after monitoring window if stable. :white_check_mark:
